evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS)

criteria.reasoning: All required elements addressed: primary mission, need (bleaching statistics, limitations of existing products), single-spacecraft justification, operator and multiple customers, funding. Detailed, well-referenced ([1]-[6]). Only minor gap: no discussion of alternative mission concepts.

evidence.quote: The baseline is an SSMS rideshare flight on Vega C from Kourou in early 2025
There are six passes each day, three in the evening and three in the morning
With a 4 m² sail the satellite re-enters about two years after the end of the mission.

criteria.reasoning: Launch site/vehicle justified with trade table and azimuth calculation; orbit elements derived by hand and verified in STK; manoeuvres explicitly addressed; ground station chosen with STK access report; data budget; five-year mission and drag-sail EOL with decay calculations. Screenshots, tables, references and appendix files all present. Link budget admittedly missing; eclipse duration treated as fixed.

evidence.quote: The design has four limitations. First, Vega C has not yet flown

criteria.reasoning: Conclusions are specific and quantitative (revisit times, pass rates, decay lifetimes) and honestly identify four limitations with proposed next steps, showing genuine design insight rather than generic summary.

evidence.quote: This report presents the design of ZYZZsat
[11] D. A. Vallado, *Fundamentals of Astrodynamics and Applications*, 4th ed.

criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with executive summary, numbered sections, consistently labelled figures/tables, all citations [1]-[15] matched to reference list, professional IEEE-style referencing, concise writing. Figures are legible STK outputs with captions. Minor: some figures low resolution; no table of contents page numbers shown.

technical_issues.issue: Eclipse duration quoted as a fixed ~34 min per orbit without considering beta-angle variation; actual eclipse time varies over the year.
X-band link budget (margin, antenna gains, data rates achievable) not performed, only data-volume budget; acknowledged by student.
Decay analysis uses single mean density and scale height; sensitivity acknowledged but lifetime estimate is crude.
Vega C unflown at time of writing; fallback given, but rideshare orbit compatibility (altitude/injection) not guaranteed.
GSD driven only by diffraction limit and pixel count; detector IFOV/sampling and pointing jitter effects on 5 m GSD not analysed.

overall: Excellent, comprehensive mission design report. All task requirements met with verified hand calculations, STK evidence, well-justified trade-offs, honest limitations, and professional presentation. Minor gaps (link budget, eclipse/beta-angle, unflown launcher) are acknowledged by the student. Approximately 9/10 on each criterion.
